title: Secondary dominants
description: Memorize V7/x construction, the five targets in major, and tonicization versus a real key change.

cards.front: What is a secondary dominant, and how is it written?
cards.back: A dominant seventh that points at a chord of the key other than the tonic. Written V7/x, “five of x”.

cards.front: In C major, why is A7 V7/ii?
cards.back: A is a fifth above D, the root of ii. A7 contains C♯, a note outside C major that acts as a leading tone to D.

cards.front: What does it mean that the target is temporarily tonicized?
cards.back: For a moment the target feels like home, without the key actually changing.

cards.front: How do you build V7/x?
cards.back: Choose a diatonic major or minor target (not the diminished chord). Find the note a perfect fifth above its root (or a fourth below). Build a dominant 7th on that note.

cards.front: Name all five secondary dominants of C major, their chords, targets, and chromatic notes.
cards.back: V7/ii A7 to Dm (C♯); V7/iii B7 to Em (D♯); V7/IV C7 to F (B♭); V7/V D7 to G (F♯); V7/vi E7 to Am (G♯).

cards.front: Why is there no V7/vii°, and what is V7/I?
cards.back: A diminished target is unstable and not a convincing temporary home. V7/I is just V7.

cards.front: In A7 (A C♯ E G) resolving to Dm, how does the tritone resolve?
cards.back: C♯ rises a half step to D, and G falls a half step to F. Both land on notes of Dm (D F A). The chromatic note is the leading tone of the target.

cards.front: Why is C7 as V7/IV the subtle case?
cards.back: E rises to F, and B♭ falls to A (the third of F). B♭ is also the note that distinguishes C7 from Cmaj7 and from the plain C triad.

cards.front: How does tonicization differ from modulation?
cards.back: Tonicization is a single chord or short phrase aimed at a target. Modulation is confirmed by more material, such as a full cadence in the new key and a lasting return to its scale. Practical test: if the original key still feels like home after the target passes, it was a tonicization.

cards.front: Is every dominant 7 a secondary dominant?
cards.back: No. A D7 in C could be V7/V resolving to G, or a color/blues chord with no target. The label requires a resolution to the target, or a clear expectation that is then deceived.

cards.front: How does I vi ii V often become a secondary-dominant chain?
cards.back: I VI7 ii V: vi is replaced by VI7 (which is V7/ii), creating VI7 to ii to V to I. In C that is C A7 Dm G7 C.

cards.front: Where are chains common, and what is a typical rock/folk use?
cards.back: Chains of secondary dominants are common in jazz standards and older popular songs. In rock and folk, a single V7/V (D7 in C) before G is typical.

cards.front: Write all five secondary dominants of G major with their targets.
cards.back: V7/ii E7 to Am; V7/iii F♯7 to Bm; V7/IV G7 to C; V7/V A7 to D; V7/vi B7 to Em.

cards.front: Write I VI7 ii V I in C, G, and F.
cards.back: C A7 Dm G7 C; G E7 Am D7 G; F D7 Gm C7 F.

cards.front: Give the open/common shapes for A7, B7, C7, D7, and E7 in C major.
cards.back: A7 x02020 (A E G C♯ E); B7 x21202 (B D♯ A B F♯); C7 x32310 (C E B♭ C E); D7 xx0212 (D A C F♯); E7 020100 (E B D G♯ B E).

cards.front: What shapes play C A7 Dm G7 C?
From A7 x02020 to Dm xx0231, which two half-step motions are on the top strings?
cards.back: C♯ on string 2 fret 2 rises to D on fret 3 (leading tone to the target root). Open high E on string 1 rises to F on fret 1 (fifth of A7 becomes the third of Dm).

cards.front: In shells A7 x0x02x to Dm7 x5x56x, where does C♯ go, and what does that remind you?
cards.back: C♯ still leads to D, but across strings and registers. Leading-tone motion is about pitch classes, not staying on one string.

cards.front: In C D7 G C, what is the target of D7, and what is its non-diatonic note?
cards.back: The target is G (V). The non-diatonic note in D7 is F♯.

cards.front: Why does C E7 Am resolve strongly while C E7 F does not?
cards.back: G♯ is the leading tone of Am and rises to A. F has no A as its root and does not receive that leading-tone resolution, so E7 is not pointing at F.

cards.front: By ear, what does C♯ add when you compare C A7 Dm with C Am Dm?
cards.back: C♯ is the extra leading tone into D. A7 tonicizes Dm; Am stays diatonic and does not pull as hard.
